newsitem.title: POLAND: LAFARGE TO BUY POLISH CEMENT PLANT STAKE.
newsitem.headline: LAFARGE TO BUY POLISH CEMENT PLANT STAKE.

text.p: Poland's National Investment Fund No. 14 has agreed to sell France's Lafarge its 33 percent stake in the Malogoszcz cement plant after a court suspended in 1996 the stake's sale to Germany's Dyckerhof , Lafarge said.
It said in a Monday statement the acqusition of the shares in Malogoszcz, in which it had already held a 41 percent stake, would give it a 25 percent share in the Polish cement market.
Lafarge also has majority stakes in Poland's Kujawy and Wierzbica cement plants. The firm did not give the value of the transaction.
"The fund and Lafarge has concluded an agreement that one of the subsidiaries of the Lafarge Group would ultimately buy a 33 eprcent stake in the Malogoszcz cement plant," the statement said.
"The agreement brings the dispute between the two sides to an end," it said.

In September 1996 Lafarge filed a complaint to a Warsaw court after NFI No. 14 said it would sell its 33 percent stake in Malogoszcz to Dyckerhoff for $35 million, even though it had already signed a tentative agreement on the sale with Lafarge.
Lafarge said in the statement it would now embark on a programme of wide modernisation of Malogoszcz to raise its productivity and quality as well as cut pollution.
